messages:
anya: Heads-up: launching a cross-model prefetch sensitivity quick-check across LL-7B, LL-13B, and LL-70B-mini quantized variants. Goal: find model-size-dependent thresholds. Small run: 500 prompts each, deterministic.

marta.g: Good. Can you standardize the metric set? p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, halluc_rate (human-eval), and token-level KL first 150 tokens.

samir: Also capture sequence-level edit-distance vs baseline for longform tasks.

ops-bot: Jobs queued: pref-sense-1789991..3 on cluster-ml-us-central.

(1h later)

ops-bot: Jobs completed. Artifacts at gs://redwood-expts/pref-sense/1789991/.

anya: Quick numbers:
- LL-7B-q4 pf=0.4: p95 160ms -> halluc 2.2% (baseline 2.1%)
- LL-13B-q4 pf=0.4: p95 210ms -> halluc 4.0% (baseline 3.9%)
- LL-70Bmini-q4 pf=0.4: p95 520ms -> halluc 7.8% (baseline 6.7%)

marta.g: So larger models show bigger quality sensitivity at the same pf=0.4. Maybe because their token-distribution shifts amplify over longer contexts.

samir: Hypothesis: bigger models with larger receptive field get more compounded bias from prefetched KV states. Need to test drop-in thresholds scaled by model depth / receptive factor.

anya: I'll run a quick scaling heuristic where pf_threshold ~ 0.4 * (7B / model_size_factor).

marta.g: Keep the notes short for the spec: model-dependent defaults and a conservative default of pf=0.3 for >30B until proven otherwise.

ops-bot: New job queued: pref-scale-heuristic-1789992.
